connector.whatItDoes: Closes the Factory1 -> Factory2 seam in two halves. PRODUCER: write-parcel-node-county.mjs walks a loaded county's txgio_parcel rows (the statewide fabric store) and emits contract-shaped parcel-node atoms into the atoms store, with typed absences, orphan retirement on re-acquire, and write-then-verify on stored bytes. CONSUMER: warm-preflight-gate.ts enforces invariant S3 — the warm set is the INTERSECTION of recipe eligibility (a zoning-fact exists) and parcel-node eligibility (a live, resolved, account-keyed anchor exists), with six named decline codes and a fail-closed arithmetic reconciliation (assertWarmGateApplied) that exits the run if any parcel reached compute without a verdict.

for the consumer: parcel-node atoms read back out of the atoms store, plus the zoning-fact recipe cohort

retired orphan rows on re-acquisition (assertNoActiveOrphans fails the run if any active orphan survives)

for the consumer: a depth-warm.parcel-node-preflight event carrying recipeCohort / anchorsFound / warmEligible / declinesByCode

blockingGaps: No source-discovery procedure for a non-Texas state. The Texas path is a single agency (TxGIO/StratMap), a single collection GUID, and a single URL template stratmap25-landparcels_{fips}_lp.zip that resolves for 253 of 254 counties with one statewide-normalized DBF schema. No document describes the discovery step that produces that finding for UT/NM/CO/AZ, and no recon note for any of the four exists. Colorado plausibly has no statewide parcel authority at all, which would break the Factory 1 premise that one source blankets a state — and nobody has checked.

A fail-closed Texas coordinate assertion sits in the acquisition hot path. assertTexasWgs84Bbox (lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/parse.ts:185) throws TxgioProjectionError on any bbox outside the Texas WGS84 envelope, and it is called per feature at parse.ts:584 and reused by the NFHL parser at nfhl/parse.ts:145. A Utah parcel would be refused ingest by design. This is correct, valuable Texas behavior and an absolute blocker for state two; it must become a per-state envelope from a registry row.

Texas coupling is pervasive in the acquisition tier: 26 of 47 non-test TypeScript files under lib/cad-ingest/src (55%) reference Texas, FIPS 48, or a texas.gov host. Hard instances include boundary/service.ts hardcoding WHERE STATE='48' for the county layer and feature.geographic.texas.gov as the host, address/service.ts pinning stratmap_address_points_48_most_recent, boundary/parse.ts defaulting stateFips to '48', and txgio/counties.ts carrying a 254-entry TXGIO_STATEWIDE_COUNTIES roster behind isTexasCountyFips. OPS-14's rule that 'no state constant may live in factory machinery' is violated throughout the tier that would have to run first.

No county-roster equivalent procedure. A new state needs its counties enumerated, FIPS-mapped, and probed before any fetch. stateFromFips already knows 48->TX, 49->UT, 16->ID, so the seam is anticipated in code — but nothing populates a roster for 49.

No per-state cost model. Commitment 3 is per-jurisdiction; Factory 1 and 1.5 costs are per-state and constant-ish, and no instrument reports them. A second-state go/no-go cannot be priced from the docs.

No Factory 1.5 runbook, so even a state whose sources were fully discovered has no acquisition procedure to follow — the operator would reverse-engineer it from lib/cad-ingest source comments and L2 wave reports.

SECONDARY, not blocking, but it would bite immediately: the promoted Factory 2 runbook still instructs the ungated legacy warm command and never mentions the parcel-node anchor prerequisite, so a competent operator following it end to end in a new state would warm parcels with no established geometry anchor and not know it.

adversarialFindings: THE CONNECTOR IS REAL — this is not a case of prose describing a nonexistent artifact. It is two committed code artifacts in hauska-engine (write-parcel-node-county.mjs, 560 lines, and src/parcel-node/ with four modules plus a contract test suite) driven by a third artifact outside any repo (run_sweep.mjs, 413 lines). The operator's belief is correct on the substance. The correction to the operator's mental model is about which HALF is proven, and about where the driver lives.

BUT THE CONNECTOR IS HALF-PROVEN, AND THE PROVEN HALF IS THE EASY HALF. The producer ran 132 counties over 46 hours in production, with independent store truth confirming 196/196 fabric counties drained. The consumer — the gate that makes the seam MEAN something — has run exactly once against real anchors, in dry mode, on 500 Elgin parcels, produced verifyPass 75 / verifyFail 98, graded its own legacy parity 'partial' rather than the 0-mismatch standard it set, left its adversarial checkpoint 'pending', and was never applied. Writing 11.6M anchors nobody has yet consumed in a promoting run is a producer achievement, not a proven seam.

THE GATE IS BYPASSABLE BY FOLLOWING THE PROMOTED RUNBOOK. gateWarmCohort is called in exactly one of four warm runners. The three legacy per-city scripts have zero calls, and 90_runbooks/factory_onboarding_runbook.md:139 — a doc with status 'active, planner-reviewed and promoted' — gives one of those legacy scripts as the verbatim Elgin command. Invariant S3 is enforced by a total function with a fail-closed arithmetic reconciliation, which is excellent engineering, and it is simply not on the documented path. This is the single most actionable finding in this inventory.

'132/132' AND '196 COUNTIES' ARE BOTH TRUE AND THE DOCS CONFLATE THEM. The runner landed 132 counties and wrote 11,060,796 atoms; the store holds 11,603,489 parcel-node atoms across 196 counties because ~64 counties were written before the sweep. _STATE.md line 23 puts both in one sentence and the FACTORY procedure doc repeats it. Anyone reading '132/132 complete' as statewide is wrong twice over: it is 196 of 254 counties, gated by 196 counties of geometry existing at all.

progress.json's failed[] ARRAY IS A RETRY LOG, NOT A HOLE — VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Three counties appear in failed[] (48277 apply-failed on a stale @empressaio/atom-contract export named OWNER_EXEMPTION_FLAGS_SCHEMA, 48265 and 48113 econnreset at attempt 4) and all three appear in landed[] with nonzero atomsWritten. I checked the resume hole directly: unique attempted = 132, landed = 132, attempted-not-landed = empty. The sweep has no hole. But the code path that permits a hole is still present, and the only defense is a manual pre-resume checklist.

THE FROZEN ARTIFACT IS UNCOMMITTED, WHICH MAKES OPERATE-NOT-REBUILD UNENFORCEABLE. The ruling with the most institutional weight in this program says: run run_sweep.mjs, change three strings, never write a new driver. That artifact exists only at P:/tmp/parcel_node_sweep_20260809/ — a path repo memory separately flags as recycle-prone. The day it is recycled, rebuilding becomes mandatory and every halt tripwire, the ECONNRESET idempotent retry, the dedup guard, and the manifest checkpointing are re-derived from a prose description or lost. Committing it is a five-minute action that protects the program's most-cited ruling.

THE ENGINE TREE POINTER IS STILL WRONG, EIGHT DAYS AFTER IT COST A RUN. P:/hauska-engine is on branch sweep/fast-write, ahead 1 and behind 4 of origin/main. run_sweep.mjs hardcodes ENGINE = P:/hauska-engine and inherits whatever that tree is checked out to. This exact trap already caused an unknown period of writing at the old 47 atoms/sec. The FACTORY procedure doc names it as an adversarial finding; it remains unfixed as of this inventory.

FACTORY 1.5 IS NOT NEW CODE — IT IS UNNAMED CODE. lib/cad-ingest in legacy-design-tools already does exactly what the operator's Factory 1.5 describes: find, fetch, parse, normalize, projection-guard, and persist with vintage provenance into txgio_parcel / txgio_address / cad_property. The retier is therefore mostly a naming, queue, and close-artifact exercise rather than a build. The honest finding is the inverse of the usual one: the operator believes a tier is NEW when the code is already there but undocumented and unqueued — which is precisely why its blockers surfaced one at a time instead of as a drainable backlog.

THE STATE-TEMPLATE CLAIM IS THE ONE PLACE WHERE A DOCUMENT ASSERTS SOMETHING THAT DOES NOT EXIST. OPS-14:86 states 'The W5 WDLL carries the template worksheet.' The W5 WDLL carries acceptance item 9 requiring a worksheet, with an empty grade box, and requires four UT/NM/CO/AZ recon notes as its evidence. No worksheet document and no recon note exists anywhere in the repo. Meanwhile _inbox/2026-08-09_W5_program_close.json declares the W5 program closed. A closed program whose acceptance card is 100% ungraded is exactly the 'a status is a claim' failure mode the factory procedure warns about.

THE GOOD NEWS ON PORTABILITY IS REAL AND WORTH STATING PRECISELY: the connector and Factory 2's engine core are clean. grep for hardcoded '48'/'TX'/texas across packages/engine-core/src returned ZERO hits outside comments, and the parcel-node module's only Texas references are explanatory comments naming Hays and Bastrop as examples. Texas constants are confined to (a) per-source adapter scripts in engine-core/scripts, which is where OPS-14's design rule says they belong, and (b) the ldt acquisition tier, where they are pervasive and where the rule is violated. So the state-portability problem is almost entirely a Factory 1.5 problem — which is a much better position than the doc set's silence would suggest, and it should shape where the template work is aimed.

NOBODY CALLS IT A CONNECTOR. Zero documents in doc_repo use the word for this seam; 'connector' there means the Revit/ArchiCAD/SketchUp/SoftPlan host-connector program. The seam is called the joint, the seam, parcel-node, Rail 1, and the C1/C5 warm preflight gate across five different documents. Adopting one name would have saved this investigation most of its search time and will save the next one the same.

ONE SIBLING WRITER CANNOT FAIL ITS OWN VERIFICATION. write-special-district-fact-county.mjs has zero atom_did IN occurrences and verifies the in-memory object it just built, so verifyFailures is structurally always 0 for that rail. It is not the connector, but it shares the connector's write-then-verify contract and is queued for the same slot — and the standing instruction to 'watch verifyFailures on the first apply' is vacuous for exactly that rail.
